title: Relay group lifecycle
description: What a roster or metadata change produces. Two things land together and describe the same mutation: a `conversation.*` event in every member's log, and a NOTICE MESSAGE in the conversation. The notice is a normal message of kind `notice`, sent by the person who did the thing — there is no system participant — with a text part for the human line and a `data` part carrying GroupMutationData. Clients render the notice from the message; the event is what tells them the roster moved.

actor.description: The person who made the change. Only humans mutate a group.

affected_participant.description: Present on every membership.* mutation; absent on group.created and metadata.updated.

mutation.description: The same object the notice message carries in its `data` part.

message.description: The notice, committed through the one message path, so every member's log, push and the conversation sequence see it exactly like any other message.

event_data.description: The `data` of the conversation.* event that accompanies the notice.

GroupMutationData.title: Group mutation
GroupMutationData.description: The structured half of a group notice: what changed, by whom. Rides as the notice message's `data` part, beside the human-readable text part.

ConversationEventData.title: conversation.* event data
ConversationEventData.description: The payload of the conversation.created / conversation.added / conversation.updated / conversation.removed / conversation.left event that accompanies the notice. The recipient's own relationship to the change picks the type: the participant who was added gets `conversation.added` (an agent) or `conversation.created` (a person), the one who left gets `conversation.left`, the one removed gets `conversation.removed`, and everybody else gets `conversation.updated`.
